## 1. The similitude in the Torah and in the Injil  (`#the-seed-in-the-torah-and-injil`)

Cited ayat: 48:29

> **48:29** مُّحَمَّدٌ رَّسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ تَرَىٰهُمْ رُكَّعًا سُجَّدًا يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنًا سِيمَاهُمْ فِى وُجُوهِهِم مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِ ذَٰلِكَ مَثَلُهُمْ فِى ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَمَثَلُهُمْ فِى ٱلْإِنجِيلِ كَزَرْعٍ أَخْرَجَ شَطْـَٔهُۥ فَـَٔازَرَهُۥ فَٱسْتَغْلَظَ فَٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِۦ يُعْجِبُ ٱلزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ ٱلْكُفَّارَ وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِنْهُم مَّغْفِرَةً وَأَجْرًا عَظِيمًۢا

### Claims

**c1** (48:29): Muhammad is the messenger of God, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves; you see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from God and approval.

**c2** (48:29): Their mark is on their faces, from the trace of prostration.

**c3** (48:29): The ayah says that this is their similitude in the Torah.

**c4** (48:29): Their similitude in the Injil is like a seed that put forth its shoot, then strengthened it, then it grew thick and stood upright on its stalk, pleasing the sowers, so that God may enrage the disbelievers through them.

**c5** (48:29): God has promised those among them who believed and did righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward.

### One-minute summary

The ayah describes those with Muhammad and says that this is their similitude in the Torah [c1][c3]. Their similitude in the Injil is like a seed that put forth its shoot and grew thick and stood upright on its stalk [c4].

### Complete story

Muhammad is the messenger of God, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves [c1]. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from God and approval [c1]. Their mark is on their faces, from the trace of prostration [c2]. The ayah says that this is their similitude in the Torah [c3].

Their similitude in the Injil is like a seed that put forth its shoot, then strengthened it, then it grew thick and stood upright on its stalk, pleasing the sowers, so that God may enrage the disbelievers through them [c4]. God has promised those among them who believed and did righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward [c5].

### Deep study

The ayah gives a description of those with Muhammad and then names the Torah and the Injil as the places for their similitude [c1][c3][c4]. The picture in the Injil is of a seed that goes through stages: a shoot, strengthening, thickening and standing upright on its stalk [c4]. The ayah ends with a promise of forgiveness and a great reward to those among them who believed and did righteous deeds [c5].

### Kids mode

The ayah says that Muhammad is the messenger of God, and that those with him are merciful among themselves [c1]. It says that you see them bowing and prostrating [c1]. Their similitude in the Injil is like a seed that put forth its shoot and grew thick and stood upright on its stalk [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture of the seed shows growth in stages, from a shoot to standing upright on its stalk [c4]. Another reading is that the ayah joins this picture to a description of those with Muhammad as bowing and prostrating and seeking bounty from God and approval [c1][c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who those with him are by name; the ayah names no one except the messenger.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later sources identify those with him with particular people and events; this draft does not repeat or vouch for them.
- Not established: what the Torah and the Injil say of them; this draft cites the Quran only and does not quote those books.
- The ayah can be read as that is their similitude in the Torah, and their similitude in the Injil is like a seed, or as one similitude stated for both books; this draft follows the first reading and leaves the other open.
- The ayah itself uses the word for a similitude (mathal) in both places.
